cleanIntro: The regular clean leaves the rifle in one piece: the bore with the bolt locked back, the magazine taken apart and washed, and the outside wiped down. Deep Clean is Remington's own takedown: action out of the stock, trigger housing off, bolt out. The book covers the Model 597 in .22 Long Rifle and the 597 Magnum in .22 Win. Mag. It does not cover a .17 HMR.

steps.title: Read the barrel: .22 LR or .22 Win. Mag.
steps.action: Read the caliber marked on the barrel before anything else. The Model 597 takes .22 Long Rifle, standard or hyper velocity. The 597 Magnum takes .22 Win. Mag. Keep all ammunition off the bench.
steps.prose: If your barrel reads .17 HMR, this book does not cover your rifle. Stop here, leave it unloaded, and ask Remington before you use it.
steps.quote: The Model 597 Magnum is designed to use .22 Win. Mag. cartridges only. The two calibers CAN NOT be interchanged. Do not use any other .22 caliber ammunition, as this can cause a jam or severe gun malfunction and result in serious personal injury or death.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Load the Firearm, WARNING, printed p.10

steps.title: Muzzle safe, red band out of sight
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and keep your finger out of the trigger guard. Push the cross-bolt button behind the trigger until you cannot see its red band. Red showing means the rifle will fire.
steps.prose: The button can be locked with the J-slot key. If it will not move, unlock it with the key; do not force it and do not poke the slot with anything else.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, push the button so the RED BAND MARKING CANNOT BE SEEN.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — The Safety Mechanism, printed p.7; The Security System, printed p.8
steps.warn: Even when the safety mechanism is engaged, careless handling can cause the firearm to fire.

steps.title: Magazine out, then the chamber
steps.action: Pull the magazine latch rearward and take the magazine out. Pull the operating handle all the way back so any cartridge in the chamber comes out. Look into the chamber, and feel it with a fingertip.
steps.prose: Magazine first: work the bolt with it still in and you may feed another round. An empty magazine well proves nothing about the chamber.
steps.quote: Visually check the chamber to make sure it is empty.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Unload the Firearm, steps 3–4, printed p.11; The Magazine, WARNING, printed p.9
steps.warn: Removing the magazine from the rifle does not prevent the rifle from being fired.

steps.title: Empty the magazine, lock the bolt back
steps.action: Away from the rifle, slide the top cartridge forward and out of the magazine, and repeat until it is empty. Put the empty magazine back in and pull the handle rearward until the bolt stays back. Look in the chamber once more, then take the magazine out.
steps.prose: The bolt holds open only when an empty magazine is in. Once it is held, the magazine can come out and the bolt stays where it is.
steps.aside: Once the last shot hold-open has been engaged, the magazine can be removed without the bolt closing.
steps.quote: Insert an empty magazine and pull the operating handle rearward until the bolt engages the last shot hold-open mechanism. Visually check the chamber to make sure the rifle is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — The Barrel, II, step 3, printed p.9; To Unload the Firearm, steps 5–6, printed p.11

steps.title: The rifle stays whole for this clean
steps.action: No screw or pin comes out for the regular clean. Remington cleans the bore with the rifle assembled and the bolt held back. Only the magazine comes apart. The takedown is in Deep Clean, and it ends where the book ends.
steps.prose: Past that point the rifle goes to the factory or a gunsmith Remington recommends.
steps.quote: rifle should not be disassembled beyond what is described in this instruction book, except by the factory
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, CAUTION, printed p.12

steps.title: Magazine bottom off, thumb on the spring
steps.action: Eye protection on. Check that the magazine is empty. Squeeze the sides of the magazine box and draw the bottom downward and off. As the spring shows, put your thumb on it and let it out slowly.
steps.prose: The spring pushes the bottom off as the sides let go. Keep it pointed away from your face.
steps.quote: Depress the sides of the magazine box and pull the magazine bottom downward and off of the magazine. As the spring becomes exposed, hold it with your thumb to prevent it from flying out.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Magazine Assembly, step 1, printed p.13
steps.warn: Use extreme care when removing the magazine bottom, as the magazine spring is under compression. Wear eye protection to avoid serious personal injury.

steps.title: Spring out, follower out
steps.action: Take out the magazine spring, then the follower. Note which end of the spring sat on the bottom before you set it down.
steps.prose: The last coil goes back over the posts on the bottom. That is how you tell the ends apart later.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Magazine Assembly, steps 2–3, printed p.13

steps.title: Wet patch through the bore
steps.action: Bolt held back, magazine out, chamber checked again. Put a patch wet with bore solvent on the rod and pass it through the bore several times. Remington names its own Brite Bore.
steps.prose: The book says to clean from the chamber end when possible. With the rifle together the rod goes in at the muzzle, so keep it centered and off the crown. Stop when the tip shows in the ejection port.
steps.quote: Pass patch through bore several times to remove loose residue and fouling
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Barrel, steps 6–7, printed p.12; The Barrel, I, step 6, printed p.9

steps.title: Brush, then patches until one comes out clean
steps.action: Fit a brush of the right caliber, wet it with the same solvent, and push it through the barrel several times. Take the brush off, then push patches through, a new one each time, until one comes out clean.
steps.prose: A .22 brush for both chamberings. Push it all the way out before you reverse it; turning the bristles around inside the bore bends them.
steps.quote: Remove the brush from the rod, attach tip with cleaning patch and push through the bore. Repeat several times, using a new cleaning patch each time until the patch is clean.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Barrel, steps 8–12, printed p.12

steps.title: Oiled patch, then a dry one
steps.action: Push one patch wet with Rem Oil through the barrel, then a clean dry patch to take the extra out. Look through the bore before you put the rod away.
steps.prose: The dry patch matters. Oil left standing in the bore is an obstruction too.
steps.quote: Push a clean dry patch through the barrel to remove excess lubricant.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Barrel, steps 13–14, printed p.12
steps.warn: After cleaning, make sure the barrel is free of obstructions.

steps.title: Magazine washed, and left dry
steps.action: Clean the magazine box and follower with a brush or cloth in warm water and dish detergent. Rinse them and dry them fully before they go back together.
steps.prose: No oil goes in here. Keep solvents that attack plastic away from it too.
steps.aside: Do not use solvents that are harmful to plastic materials.
steps.quote: Clean the magazine and follower with brush or cloth in warm water and household dishwashing detergent. Do not use lubricant in magazine.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Magazine Assembly, step 4, printed p.13; Loading the Magazine, printed p.10

steps.title: Outside: one light coat, and no more
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrel and the outside metal with a light coat of Rem Oil on a soft clean cloth. If the rifle went into salt water, flush every part with fresh water first, then dry, clean and oil it as soon as you can.
steps.prose: For storage, clean it carefully and oil it thoroughly. Before you use it again, take all the extra oil off and swab the chamber and bore clean and dry.
steps.quote: Over-lubrication should be avoided at all times.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — Lubrication, printed p.12; Cleaning, Lubrication and Maintenance, WARNING, printed p.11
steps.warn: Excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could adversely affect the function and safe operation of your rifle.

steps.title: Look it over, and know when it is due
steps.action: With the bolt held back, look over the bore, the bolt face and as much of the inside as you can see. You want it clean, with no rust and no grit. Clean the whole rifle before and after long storage and at least once a year.
steps.prose: If it has not worked right, it goes to a gunsmith before it is fired again. Remington also wants it professionally serviced every year.
steps.aside: Remington recommends that you have your firearm professionally serviced annually.
steps.quote: Periodically inspect the internal workings of your firearm to be sure they're clean and free of rust, unwanted dirt and debris.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — 9th Commandment, printed p.6; maintenance and care, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: Unloaded, magazine out, bolt let forward
deepSteps.action: Eye protection on. Safety on, red band hidden. Magazine out of the rifle, and the chamber and action checked empty by eye. Then pull back on the operating handle and let the bolt go forward.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt is forward for the whole takedown. Keep your fingers out of the ejection port as it runs home.
deepSteps.quote: Pull rearward on operating handle and release the bolt forward
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, steps 1–4, printed p.12
deepSteps.warn: Always wear eye protection when disassembling and reassembling the firearm.

deepSteps.title: Two takedown screws, 1/8 inch Allen
deepSteps.action: Turn out the front and rear takedown screws on the underside of the stock with a 1/8 inch Allen wrench. Lay them down in order, front and rear.
deepSteps.prose: The parts list gives a front screw and a rear screw as separate parts, so do not mix them.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the front and rear takedown screws, using a 1/8" Allen Wrench.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, step 5, printed p.12; parts list, printed p.17

deepSteps.title: Action up and out of the stock
deepSteps.action: Lift the action out of the stock and set the stock aside.
deepSteps.prose: What is in your hand is two major parts still pinned together: the receiver assembly and the housing assembly. The housing holds the trigger.
deepSteps.quote: Lift and remove the action from the stock.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, step 6 and NOTE, printed pp.12–13

deepSteps.title: Tap out the one assembly pin
deepSteps.action: Tap the assembly pin out of the receiver. It comes out from either side, so use whichever is easier to support.
deepSteps.prose: This single pin holds the rear of the housing. Use a punch that fits it and light taps.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, step 7, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Swing the housing down and away
deepSteps.action: Rotate the rear of the housing downward. It pivots around its front end. Go slowly until it separates from the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: A key on the front of the housing sits in a slot in the barrel extension. Pulling straight down fights it; rotating lets it out.
deepSteps.quote: separating the housing from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning, step 8, printed p.13
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT PULL TRIGGER WHILE HOUSING IS OUT OF FIREARM.

deepSteps.title: Guide rail screws out, rails walked back
deepSteps.action: Take the two guide rail screws out of the rear of the receiver. Then cycle the bolt several times until the guide rails stick out of the rear of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt does the work of moving the rails. Do not pry on them.
deepSteps.quote: Remove two guide rail screws from rear of receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Receiver/Barrel Assembly, steps 1–2, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Guide rails out, springs under control
deepSteps.action: Eye protection on. Pull the guide rails out one at a time, keeping a grip on the action spring on each. A .22 LR rifle has one spring on each rail; the Magnum has an inner and an outer on each.
deepSteps.prose: Keep each rail's springs with it as they come out.
deepSteps.quote: Pull bolt guide rails out. Care should be taken with guide rail springs.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Receiver/Barrel Assembly, step 3, printed p.13; parts lists, printed p.17
deepSteps.warn: The action springs are under compression. A rail let go can throw its spring.

deepSteps.title: Handle out, then the bolt
deepSteps.action: Pull the operating handle outward, out of the bolt. Then take the bolt out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The strip ends here. The bolt itself, with its firing pin and extractor, is not taken apart by this book.
deepSteps.quote: Pull out on operating handle to remove handle from bolt. Remove bolt from receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Receiver/Barrel Assembly, steps 4–5, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Inside the receiver and the end of the barrel
deepSteps.action: Brush the inside of the receiver and the end of the barrel with gun cleaning solvent and wipe them dry. Then put a light coat of Rem Oil on the inside of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Light means a film. Rimfire residue sticks to wet oil and turns to paste.
deepSteps.quote: Brush the inside of the receiver and end of the barrel with gun cleaning solvent and wipe dry.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Receiver/Barrel Assembly, steps 6–7, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: The housing, cleaned as one unit
deepSteps.action: Safety on, red band hidden. Spray the housing with Rem Action Cleaner and let it dry. Spray Rem Oil on the hammer and the trigger linkage, let it stand 15 minutes, and spray again to wash it off. Wipe or blow off what is left.
deepSteps.prose: Nothing comes out of the housing. The trigger stays untouched until the housing is back in the receiver.
deepSteps.aside: Wipe or blow off excess lubricant.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT PULL TRIGGER WHILE HOUSING IS OUT OF FIREARM.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 597 & 597 Magnum Rimfire Autoloading Rifles — ABSENT — no edition, revision or form number is printed on any scanned page — To Clean the Housing Assembly, CAUTION and steps 1–3, printed p.13; The Trigger Assembly, WARNING, printed p.9
deepSteps.warn: NEVER alter or modify any part of the trigger assembly or any part of the firing mechanism.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bolt held back, magazine out, chamber checked again
Brush through several times, then patches until one is clean
One oiled patch, then one dry patch
⛔ Bore looked through: nothing left in it

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Box and follower washed in warm water and dish detergent

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE AND STORAGE
tasks: Outside metal wiped with a light coat of oil
Wet in salt water: fresh-water flush first, then dry, clean and oil
Before use after storage: extra oil off, chamber and bore dry

reassembly: ⛔ Check the chamber and the magazine box: no cartridges anywhere in the rifle. Magazine box out of the rifle until the action is back in the stock. Eye protection on.
Bolt into the receiver, bolt face toward the barrel. Slide it forward until it touches the barrel.
Guide rails into the rear of the receiver until they stick out about 1/2 inch from its inside face.

Put one action spring (the inner and outer set on a .22 Win. Mag.) into the recess of the bolt and over the guide rail. Work the spring over the rail while you push the rail toward the barrel. The rail slides through the slot on the side of the bolt. Do the same on the other side.
Operating handle through the ejection port and into the bolt.
Pull the bolt rearward and check that the guide rails are held in the barrel extension.
Guide rail screws in, tightened with a torque wrench to 10–12 in-lb.
Spray the guide rails lightly with Rem Oil. The bolt must slide freely in the receiver. ⛔ If it does not, stop and find out why.
Key on the front of the housing into its slot in the barrel extension. Rotate the rear of the housing into the receiver, line up the assembly pin holes, and put the assembly pin in.
Action into the stock. ⛔ Safety on, red band hidden.
Front and rear takedown screws in, both tightened with the 1/8 inch Allen wrench to 45 in-lb.
Magazine, if it was taken apart: follower in, then the spring with its coils lined up as they came out. Posts of the bottom into the last coil, and push the bottom on until it snaps.
fncheck: No ammunition near the rifle, safety on with the red band hidden, empty magazine in. Pull the operating handle rearward: the bolt slides freely and stays back on the hold-open. With no magazine in, the bolt will not hold open; that is how it is made. Look through the bore once more. The book prints no other check, and this one never asks you to pull the trigger.
reassemblyRoutine: Magazine follower back into the box.
Spring in, with its coils lined up as they came out. Posts of the magazine bottom into the last coil of the spring.
Push the bottom onto the box until it snaps into place.
⛔ Chamber and magazine checked: no cartridges. Safety on, red band hidden.
Empty magazine back into the rifle.
